#### Stocks seesaw starts? 



- LME copper has risen above $8,000/t in the New Year, following the general market buoyancy as the US “fiscal cliff” deadline passed without triggering massive spending cuts and tax hikes. However, while tax hikes have been agreed, spending cuts and the raising of the debt ceiling have yet to be resolved, clouding sentiment for Q1 and Q2. 



- While most of the market has observed the seasonal quiet, we note that spot activity has apparently picked up in China, and bonded stock levels are reported to have fallen for the first time since last June.  This is despite the proximity to the Lunar New Year, which usually inspires slowing activity. 



- Elsewhere, LME stocks continue to rise, and the Western markets are mainly quiet as the New Year begins.  2013 long-term contract volumes are said to be “roughly the same” as last year.

Forecas|t productio|n allows| © 2013 CRU International Limited **confidential** Copper Monitor February 2013 www.crugroup.com #### Price follows but lags “fiscal cliff” gains The price rally which began in mid-November was LME not as buoyant as stock checked in late December by concerns over the US markets “fiscal cliff” situation, as wrangling over the terms of Daily LME copper cash price, S&P 500 index the deal continued until the eleventh hour. However, 8500 1,510 US politicians were eventually able to agree on certain 1,490 key points, including tax increases for the wealthy, and 8250 1,470 1,450 postponed the decision on other elements for another 8000 1,430 two months, allowing the deadline to pass without 1,410 triggering the high taxes and heavy spending cuts that 7750 1,390 were scheduled to occur on 1st January otherwise. The 1,370 7500 1,350 markets responded, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average closing up 300 points on 2nd January and other stock markets showing similar enthusiasm, particularly LME Copper Cash, ($/t), LHS S&P 500 index, RHS in the US. Amidst the general wave of relief, commodities were not left out; with LME 3-month Data: LME, S&P copper gaining $180/t to reach over $8,100/t on the same day. However, as the chart indicates, LME copper has struggled to maintain the same buoyancy seen elsewhere. Although the price remained above the $8,000/t mark for another eight trading days, sobriety was even then slowly returning and, despite recent gains, the trend line so far in January is still pointing back to below the $8,000/t line. Despite the boost from the part resolution of the “fiscal cliff”, the fact remains that some particularly contentious aspects of the US’s new budget deal have yet to be resolved. Republicans and Democrats are believed to be still some distance apart in their positions on the raising of the debt ceiling and, critically, the level of government spending cuts that are to take place. Although a bill to temporarily extend the debt ceiling until May was passed in the last 24 hours, alleviating some tension, the new deadline for the automatic spending cuts is 1st March, and current funding for the government is set to run out on 27th March. The spectre of a US default has now been pushed out to Q2, but we still feel that a repeat of the depressed investor sentiments seen in late December is likely to be seen in February, as the political tussle ov

er spending cuts reaches fever pitch. #### Seasonal lull for most… Meanwhile, in the copper market, the traditional seasonal quiet continues, with a lot of funds “waiting on the sidelines”, according to one market insider, and producers and consumers cautiously eyeing the year ahead. Amongst producers, widespread expectations of a refined surplus this year foster watchfulness, while consumers everywhere hope for a better 2013. On the physical side, we are told that most market participants have committed to 2013 contract volumes that are “roughly the same” as 2012 volumes, though in China, rumours persist that some buyers have committed to lower tonnages. Amongst consumers outside China, we hear that most are aiming to get by on their long term contract tonnages this © 2013 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 2 of 20 Copper Monitor February 2013 www. crugroup.com year, with the spot market considered somewhat risky due to availability concerns, in part driven by last year’s apparent scarcities. That being said, it is our understanding that premiums have recently fallen in Europe, on the back of “a surprising amount of material being offered around”, according to one consumer we spoke to. Numbers varied, since no one we spoke to claimed to have done any actual business, but the premiums are now agreed to be well below the $80/t still seen towards the end of last year. (US premiums are also down a little, moving close to 6¢/lb.) It is not immediately clear where this material has sprung from. Some theorised that it might have come out of the LME warehouses, since it was being offered CIF Rotterdam. However, LME tonnages in Europe have been rising rather than falling of late, as the accompanying chart clearly indicates. Could it be that consumption is a little soft? It is certainly a weak time of year for industrial production, and the price gains in Exchange stocks build - bonded

December and January may have encouraged some downstream purchasers to delay. Given the short lead times being seen in the markets for most semis, such a reaction by semis consumers could have a fairly swift effect on refined copper consumption. However, European consumers have talked of slowly increasing demand since the low point of September/October last year. At this stage, it seems too early to tell, and some participants expressed the view that the decline in premiums could be temporary: In a paucity of real business being done, one trade can be wield disproportionate, but short-lived, influence. In

China, the seasonal lull is being observed by the funds and the consumers, who are being fairly typically inactive in the lead up to the Lunar New Year holiday. As noted in our CCF publication last Friday, those downstream manufacturers that rely heavily on migrant workers will be closing during the festive period for 2-3 weeks. #### …but something may be changing in China However, unusually for this time of year, according to our conversations with market participants in China, premiums have moved up due to an uptick in spot activity. Simultaneously, we hear that the bonded stock levels in China (in both Shanghai and Guangdong) have edged downwards for the first time since June 2012, by around 60,000t to a total level of around 765,000t. The surface explanations given for both events seem to be conflicting at first. Spot business is said to have picked up because many buyers opted to reduce their long-term contract volumes in 2013. However, a number of people that we spoke to have cited the arbitrage between SHFE and the LME provoking material to move out of China and into the LME warehouses of Asia. Comparing the recent © 2013 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 3 of 20 Copper Monitor February 2013 www.crugroup.com price moves by the two big exchanges, we can see that the relief apparently felt by LME investors over the “fiscal cliff” deadline passing was not shared by SHFE investors. This makes sense given that the SHFE price is more closely related to physical activity, which in most parts of the world starts the year relatively sluggishly. Though the LME price has fallen back somewhat since then, the SHFE price has been flat, preserving the arbitrage so far this month. If the arbitrage is the reason, then there is a motivation to export the bonded material, but then it would be accordingly discouraged from “entering” China (by paying duty and entering the nonbonded warehouses) to service the requirements of the spot market. Moreover, the arbitrage has been less extreme than the levels seen in December, during which time bonded stocks continued to rise. SHFE price did not share LME's

The data for certain LME warehouses in Asia show rising copper volumes so far in January, which indicates the destination for at least some of the material leaving the bonded warehouses. Moreover, this correlates with conversations we have had with certain cathode exporters, who have told us that increasingly they are receiving requests from buyers to switch their delivery contract destinations from the usual C

IF Shanghai, to CIF Busan in Korea or to the Malaysian ports, on a freight parity basis. We note that the queuing periods for copper in some of these warehouses are amongst the lengthiest. We could then theorize that if the arbitrage is no better than a month ago, then is the true motivation to export from China part of another backwardation push by certain interested parties? If so, the decision to rely Stocks build in certain

On the other hand, many Chinese buyers are said to have retreated from their previous volumes on long-term contracts, and some of these companies will be the same people exporting the bonded material, or diverting incoming cargoes to the LME. Therefore, it would not be logical to try to drive a backwardation. Considering all these factors, it seems that the most likely explanation for the falling bonded stocks is the tightening of credit availability in China for metal financiers that has been taking place. The restrictions being placed by Chinese banks on the issuing of letters of credit is now beginning to take its toll, with limits © 2013 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 4 of 20 Copper Monitor February 2013 www. crugroup.com being placed on the ability to utilise copper cathode in the bonded warehouses for financing deals. This is now beginning to undercut the liquidity required to keep rolling the metal financing along, and so the stock build has been checked and existing collateral stocks are now being moved, mainly to the LME, since the arbitrage is in favour of exports, but some “into” China, hence the SHFE non-bonded stocks creeping up slightly. Further tonnages that were headed for the bonded warehouses are now apparently being diverted, such as the shipments switching from Shanghai to other ports mentioned above. #### Physically-backed copper ETFs face more opposition The saga continues in the story of the attempt to introduce physically-backed copper ETFs, with a delayed ruling and further open protest from the group of US-based copper consumers and one physical copper merchant that have been opposed to the scheme since the beginning. Following JP Morgan’s 62,000t XF Physical Copper Trust fund gaining approval in mid-December, the SEC then decided a week later to delay a decision on an application by Blackrock Asset Management for a similar, larger ETF holding (namely the “iShares Copper Trust”, able to hold up to 121,000 tonnes of copper) until 22nd February. It is not clear under what grounds the SEC has decided on this postponement. In the latest development, around a week ago, the group o

f copper consumers that are in opposition to JP Morgan’s fund have written an open letter to the SEC, criticising its decision to allow the fund as “arbitrary and capricious”, and calling for them to reverse it. An appeal against the SEC’s decision now looks likely, and this may further delay the ruling on Blackrock’s fund. The key contention from the group of consumers is that the funds will remove sufficient volumes of physical copper from the market to threaten the ability of the US copper industry to obtain material in a timely manner and at acceptable prices. While “acceptable” is clearly subjective, the consumers can make an argument about the fluidity of the market affecting their bottom lines: They can point to the fact that physical delivery was hampered last year enough to support relatively strong premiums in Europe and the US, despite the market not being in a clear deficit. #### Price heading down in Q1 to average <$8,000/t The copper price has spent the past few days above $8,000/t, following a move below this level a week ago. While this seems positive, we are not convinced that there is sufficient momentum to keep the price with an “8” in front of it for too long. From a copper-specific angle, the recent build-up in LME stocks, plus anecdotal evidence from our conversations with market insiders, indicate that there has been a softening of the market ex-China. We also note that SHFE prices have been flat, despite an uptick in spot activity, while the LME price trend still points downward so far this year, despite recent gains. Looking at broader drivers, the combined effects of nervous investors awaiting a final resolution of the “Fiscal Cliff”, and the annual loosening of the physical market when virtually the whole of China downs tools for its Lunar New Year Festival, should add to the copper-specific factors to exert downward pressure on the price during Q1. For these reasons, we are expecting the price to average less than $8,000/t this quarter. © 2013 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 5 of 20 Copper Monitor February 2013 www.crugroup.com ### Consumption trends #### Growth in wirerod consumption remains subdued Wirerod demand bumping along
Quarterly data Q1 2009 - Q4 2012
The growth in world wirerod consumption slowed in 2012 in line with a more challenging environment in certain key consuming regions. CRU estimates that global consumption of wirerod increased 2.8% y-o-y in 2012, reaching 14.97Mt. The fourth quarter saw a slight pickup in growth, with consumption expanding 3.0% y-o-y, compared to 2.6% y-o-y in the third quarter. Growth by region has been varied; we note continued weakness in Western Europe and North East Asia, offset by stronger consumption in Mexico, Brazil and reasonably strong consumption in China. 15%

Chinese consumption of wirerod is estimated to have World IP y-o-y% increased by 4.8% y-o-y in 2012, helped by a pickup in World wirerod consumption y-o-y% the final quarter of 2012 as fixed asset investment Data: CRU accelerated. Whilst this is lower than the double digit increase in consumption recorded between 2007 and 2010, it still marks a pickup from 2011. Fixed asset investment in real estate continued to gather pace in the fourth quarter, with a three month moving average of the growth in China’s real estate investment rebounding from a low of 18.1% y-o-y in August 2012, to 25.1% y-o-y in November. This has helped lift demand for building wire in the fourth quarter. Autos production in China also picked up in 2012, growing by 6.5% and boosting demand for automotive wiring harnesses. While again this growth is slower than the levels seen in 2010, we still note a gentle acceleration compared with 2011. Despite a moderate recovery in wirerod consumption in China, sentiment has failed to keep pace with the slight improvement in the outlook for wirerod demand. We note in recent months that the rapid expansions of capacity in China have intensified competition and eroded margins since 2011. A survey of Chinese wirerod producers by the **Shanghai Metals Market** showed that utilisation rates averaged 72% in 2012, five percentage points lower than the 77% seen in 2011. Despite this, we believe the ramp up in Chinese wirerod production capacity is continuing apace, with more capacity expected online in 2013. In recent weeks, we have heard of a string of new wirerod projects expected to come online in China in 2013, including a 220,000t production ramp up at a large Chinese wirerod producer in Jiangsu. In terms of 2013, our conversations with market participants in China suggest the first two months of the year, until after Chinese New Year, are likely to see weak demand for wirerod. This is because cable makers suffer from a seasonal downturn in demand, exacerbated by cold weather in northern China which suppresses the demand for underground cables. One of our contacts believes that industry-wide operating © 2013 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 6 of 20 Copper Monitor February 2013 www. crugroup.com rates could be as low as 40% during the period. He also said that he does not believe the demand for wirerod will pick up until after the Chinese New Year when cable producers will restock. #### Wirerod consumption continues to decline in W.Europe Total Western European consumption of wirerod continued its downward slide in 2012, although the market was mixed with some countries faring worse than others. Europe’s largest economy, Germany, saw consumption of wirerod slide by 1.0% in 2012. This decline was linked to weakness in major enduse sectors. CRU’s central macroeconomic f

orecast team estimate that autos production was down by 6% in Germany in 2012, hitting the demand for copper wire used in automotive wiring harnesses. The demand for building wire was also weak in the fourth quarter, with the **Markit** German PMI construction index for December falling to a 10-month low. The home appliance manufacturing sector, another enduser of copper wire, fared slightly better with growth of 0.6% according to **Zentralverband Elektrotechnik- und Elektronikindustrie e.V. (ZVEI)** . The growth was driven by domestic consumption, rather than export markets, with export shipments falling 2% in 2012. French consumption of copper wirerod has bucked the trend of European wirerod demand, and wider French economic conditions, with the growth in the consumption of wirerod estimated at 0.6% y-o-y in 2012. **Nexans** , the wire and cable maker, which has significant operations in France, announced that revenues, at constant metals prices, in the first nine months of 2012 increased by 6.8% compared to the 2011. According to company results, sales growth increased in the industrial cables and distributors and installers sectors, both of which use copper wirerod to Italian wirerod demand lags some extent. Of the countries in North America, US consumption of wirerod decreased by 1.6% y-o-y in 2012, whilst Mexican consumption increased by 8.7% y-o-y. However, these figures are misleading, because Mexico is a large base for US manufacturing of automotive wiring harnesses. Almost all vehicle harnesses used in the US are imported and over 80% of these imports come from Mexico. CRU’s central macroeconomic team estimates that US autos production increased by 10% in 2012, suggesting a large part of the jump in Mexican consumption of wirerod was US-led. In other news, we heard in December that the new US-based **SDI La Farga** wirerod plant, which is entirely fed by No.2 scrap, has so far only received limited orders. An official from the company said that it was waiting for more orders to increase production. We are also hearing from some downstream producers that they are expecting a demand pick up as part of the reconstruction effort following ‘Superstorm Sandy,’ this could impact wirerod consumption in 2013. #### Japanese autos production supports consumption Japanese wirerod consumption proved more resilient than in fellow North Asian markets in 2012, as the Japanese autos sector staged a recovery in production; CRU estimates production of autos was up 18% y- o-y in 2012. Japanese wirerod consumption is estimated to have increased by 2.7% in 2012, despite a troubled Q4 for the nation’s wire and cable makers, which saw **Hitachi Cable** undergo a restructuring. South Korean and Taiwanese consumption of wirerod was less robust in 2012, falling 5.5% y-o-y and 4.2% y-o-y respectively. We believe exports from these countries were under pressure in 2012; and this is particularly true for cable exporters to China, where expansions to domestic capacity have occurred. © 2013 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 8 of 20 Copper Monitor February 2013 www. crugroup.com ### Industry N

#### Consumption 



- **Jiangsu Jiangrun Copper Co. Ltd** , a large Chinese copper wirerod producer, is planning to increase production of copper wirerod to 500,000t in 2013, up from 280,000t in 2012, according to an official from the company.  The official said copper wirerod demand was weak in 2012, and that the company's output fell by 68,000t from 2011.  Jiangsu Jiangrun has invested in a new copper wirerod project which will come online from June 2013, giving the company another 350,000t/y of capacity, which will take total capacity to 750,000t/y. 



- According to data from the **Copper and Brass Servicenter (CBSA)** , shipments from US brass and copper mills fell 8.6% m-o-m in November, to 20.5Mlb (9,300t).  The organisation said that total shipments in the first 11 months of the year were broadly unchanged from 2011, at 244.8Mlb (111,000t).  A breakdown of the figures reveals that copper sheet and copper wirerod saw the smallest declines in the month, -5.2% m-o-m and -5.3% m-o-m respectively, whilst brass sheet was the worst performing sector recording an output drop of 11.7% m-o-m. 



- Brazilian copper and alloy semis manufacturer **Termomecanica** is planning to invest BRL300M (US$143M) in several new products and production facilities.  The plans will see the company develop a new line of tube and rolled products, as well as new brass rebar production facilities in Chile and Argentina.  The company said that its current production capacity is 140,000 t/y, and that it is producing about 90,000 t/y at the moment.  An official from the company said that **Termomecanica** believes that both the Brazilian market, and export markets, will grow. 



- According to Tetsu Takahashi, chairman of the **Japan Copper & Brass Association** , Japanese production of copper and alloy semi-finished products will total 770,000t in 2012, the lowest level since 2009.  However, the association is more positive on the prospects for 2013 suggesting that output could expand by 4%, supported by a weaker yen and more accommodative government policies.  The association believes that the new government's efforts to reconstruct areas damaged by the 2011 earthquake, as well as the possibility for a rebound in autos exports to China, should lift the demand for Japanese semis in 2013. 



- Physical copper consumers, including **AmRod Corp.** , **Southwire Co** and **Encore Wire Corp.** are setting the stage for another confrontation with the SEC over the controversial approval of **JP Morgan's** physically-backed copper ETF.  In an open letter to the SEC from the group's lawyers, they reiterated claims that the ETF would leave less copper in the market for manufacturers, creating shortages and boosting prices.  According to a report from the **Financial Times** , it is now thought likely that the group of consumers will appeal the SEC decision.  The SEC has postponed its decision on whether to allow **Blackrock** to launch a physically backed ETF for two mo

nths, the decision is now scheduled for 22<sup>nd</sup> February.

#### Mine Production 



- Workers at **Southern Copper** ’s Peruvian operations staged a two-day general strike on 24<sup>th</sup> -25<sup>th</sup> December.  This followed the failure of wage talks with the operator over a new labour contract, which began in August 2012.  Further talks began on 7<sup>th</sup> January, with workers asking for a 15% wage increase compared to the company’s offer of 5.5%.  No agreement was reached and workers will vote on 23<sup>rd</sup> January to decide on future strike action.  Southern Copper operates the **Cuajone** and **Toquepala** mines, as well as the **Ilo** smelter in Peru. 



- An early pay offer to workers at the **Escondida mine** by mine operator **BHP Billiton** was rejected at the end of December 2012 as it was considered to be inadequate.  The union will vote on a revised proposal on 24<sup>th</sup> January.  The contract does not expire until the end of June 2013, however.  If an early agreement is not reached, then collective negotiations will begin in July, and strike action before then would be illegal. 



- **Codelco** will submit a plan for three natural gas-fired power plants with total generating capacity of 780MW for environmental approval in the coming weeks.  The project, known as **Luz Minera** , will involve investment of USD758M.  Once permits are in place, the company will launch an international tender for the development phase.  The plants will be at Mejillones in northern region II and provide power to the company’s **Chuquicamata** , **Gaby, Radomiro Tomic** and **Ministro Hales** divisions.  In September, the company awarded a contract for a 32MW solar plant to heat water needed for SXEW operations at Gaby. 



- It was announced on 22<sup>nd</sup> January that the **South African regulatory authorities** have approved the merger between **Glencore** and **Xstrata** , which is now just awaiting Chinese approval.  The South African tribunal attached conditions limiting job losses following the merger.  Xstrata and Glencore have pushed out the deadline for the merger from 31<sup>st</sup> January to 15<sup>th</sup> March. 

#### Exploration and Development 



- Commissioning of the concentrator at **Turquoise Hill Resources’ Oyu Tolgoi** mine began in late December 2012 and first concentrate is now expected to be produced by the end of January. Commercial production is expected to follow within three to five months.  Initial production will be at a rate of around 150,000t/y copper-in-concentrate. 



- The start-up of production at **Lumina Copper’s Caserones** mine project in Chile will be delayed until February 2013 due to a stoppage by subcontractors.  Workers have demanded days off for the Christmas and New Year public holidays when their contracts specify 10 days on duty and 10 days off.  At the

beginning of the year, only 900 employees were working, out of a total of 18,000.  The workers were granted the days off, but the stoppages meant that many workers were off for around 3 weeks in total.

- **Chinalco Peru Copper** has announced that it is targeting Q4 2013 for the start-up of operations at its **Toromocho** mine in Peru, with full production of 250,000t/y of copper-in-concentrates to be achieved by Q3 2014.  The company has also disclosed that it has signed offtake agreements for 60% of the mine’s output, with buyers including major trading companies **Trafigura** and **Louis Dreyfus** , Chinese trading company **Hongfan International** and Chinese smelting company **Tongling Nonferrous Metals** . 

- The **Peruvian government** has approved the necessary licenses for **Anglo American** to move ahead with its **Quellaveco** project, and preliminary work is reported to have begun.  The company has also worked out an agreement with the local community over water usage in the region.  However, a decision by the board on whether to go ahead with the project, which will cost more than USD3B to develop, was delayed from December 2012 until the next board meeting in March or April due to management changes in 2013.  Construction will take around 44 months, and production will average 220,000t/y of copper-in-concentrate. 

- **Antofagasta Minerals** has suspended development at its **Antucoya** project in Chile in order to complete a review of the project’s operating and capital costs.  A revised cost estimate has put capital costs at more than USD1.85B for the mine project (USD2.25B including an acid plant). The mine will produce 80,000t/y of EW cathode over a 20-year mine life based on current reserves.  Start up was scheduled for the second half of 2014. 

- On 9<sup>th</sup> January, **Tiger Resources** announced the positive results for the definitive feasibility study for stage 2 of its **Kipoi** copper project, and on 17<sup>th</sup> January, a turnkey contract was awarded to **SENET** for the construction of the plant.  The project involves the construction of 50,000t/y SXEW facility to replace the current heavy media separation (HMS) unit.  The HMS is currently producing 36,000t/y of copper in a 25% concentrate.  Initially, both facilities will operate simultaneously, but the SXEW will supersede the HMS in Q2 2014.  For the first 2½ years, the SXEW plant will process residues from the HMS during which time mining operations will cease. 

- Zambian power provider **Copperbelt Energy** is planning to build a 35km overhead transmission line to **First Quantum’s Sentinel** mine project in Solwezi.  The power will be taken from a hydropower station to a **ZESCO** substation located at the mine site.  Copperbelt Energy is the sole provider of power to mines in the Zambian copperbelt and has a bulk agreement

with state utility company ZESCO.  Construction of the power line is expected to take 12 months at a cost of MWK68.87B (USD13M). 

- **Codelco** has submitted a new EIS for its **Andina mine** expansion project, now expected to begin construction in 2014.  The original EIS was submitted in September 2011, but withdrawn soon after.  New elements in the revised EIS include an ore transport and storage system.  The expansion will lift ore production from 92,000t/d to 244,000t/d, adding 350,000t/y of fine copper to the division’s output.

- Japanese companies **Sumitomo Corp.** and **Sumitomo Metal Mining** have agreed to take a combined share of 15% in the expansion of **Freeport McMoRan’s Morenci** mine in the USA, the same as their current equity stake in the mine. The Japanese companies will contribute USD260M to the USD1.7B capital required.  Annual production will increase to 400,000t/y from current levels of around 280,000t/y, of which 215,000t is EW cathode and 65,000t is in concentrates.  The additional production will be copper-in-concentrate. 



- **Southern Copper** has reported that it has reached an agreement with a local community in Tacna province that will allow it to move ahead with the expansion of its **Toquepala mine** .  The company has agreed to create a development fund of USD100M for the community, and will also undertake studies on potential new water sources for the farmers in the region.  The expansion will lift output by 100,000t/y of copper-in-concentrate.  Negotiations are continuing with communities in Moquegua over the planned expansion of the **Cuajone** mine. 



- **Gecamines** has announced plans for a 200,000t/y metallurgical plant to process ores from the **Deziwa** and **Ecaille C** copper-cobalt deposits in the DRC, acquired from the buyout of **Copperbelt Minerals** .  The two deposits are estimated to contain 5Mt of copper.  The plant will be built in two phases with the first 100,000t/y phase expected to cost USD0.8-1B.  The company has initiated discussions with banks over financing for the project. 

#### Smelting and Refining 



- **Pan Pacific Copper** has announced planned maintenance closures at its **Saganoseki** and **Tamano** smelters in the fiscal year starting 1<sup>st</sup> April.  Saganoseki will be closed for 2 weeks from 1<sup>st</sup> April and for a further 40 days from 1<sup>st</sup> November, while Tamano will be closed for 35 days from 13<sup>th</sup> March 2014.  However the company has stated that there will be no impact on refined copper production and sales.  Tamano was closed for 1 month in Q4 2012.
